BURSEVI:v9p237/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p237/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p237/r5.claim: ‘He raised the heaven’ means God created it visibly elevated in place and rank, as the source of His judgments and commands and the abode of angels.
BURSEVI:v9p237/r5.anchor: خلقها مرفوعة محلا كما هو محسوس مشاهد وكذا رتبة

BURSEVI:v9p237/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p237/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p237/r6.claim: Others explain the raising as lifting heaven above earth to serve as a roof for creatures, with five hundred years’ distance between them; heaven was smoke evaporated above the earth’s water.
BURSEVI:v9p237/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : رفعها من السفل إلى العلو سقفا لمصالح العباد

BURSEVI:v9p237/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p237/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p237/r7.claim: ‘He set the balance’ means instituting justice: giving each deserving person their due and each rights-holder their right so the world remains ordered; a Prophetic saying links the order of heaven and earth to justice.
BURSEVI:v9p237/r7.anchor: أي شرع العدل وأمر به بأن وفر كل مستحق لما استحقه

BURSEVI:v9p237/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p237/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p237/r8.claim: Other interpretations identify the balance as the Quran or as instruments such as scales and measures by which people know quantities and fulfill just dealings; Sa‘di al-Mufti and al-Zamakhshari favor the concrete measuring sense in context.
BURSEVI:v9p237/r8.anchor: قيل فعلى هذا الميزان هو القرآن وقيل هو ما يعرف به مقادير الأشياء من ميزان وميكال ونحوهما

QASHANI:55:8-9/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:8-9/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:8-9/r1.claim: The sky is intellect raised toward spirit and heart; justice is the balance lowered to self and body, necessary for human virtue and bodily and spiritual order.
QASHANI:55:8-9/r1.anchor: أي: سماء العقل { رفعها } إلى محل شمس الروح وثمر القلب

QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r5.claim: God raised and ordered the sky, set its stars, protected it from disorder, and fixed its horizons; He created the balance for fairness in human dealings.
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r5.anchor: وخلق الميزان بين الناس ليعتبروا الإنصاف في المعالملات بينهم

QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r6.claim: Another interpretation makes the balance justice itself.

TUSTARI:55:7/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:55:7/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:55:7/r1.claim: The inner meaning of the balance is God's commands and prohibitions governing the limbs.
TUSTARI:55:7/r1.anchor: قال: باطنها الأمر والنهي على الجوارح.

FARRA:v3p112#2/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p112#2/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p112#2/r2.claim: The balance set in the earth is justice.

FARRA:v3p112#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p112#2/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p112#2/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads وخفض الميزان; lowering and setting the balance are close in meaning.
FARRA:v3p112#2/r3.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله: وخفض الميزان، والخفض والوضع

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#5/r1.claim: The balance God set is justice on earth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r1.claim: Fronting “the heaven” before its governing verb heightens attention to reflection on its creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r1.anchor: وتقديم السماء على الفعل الناصب له زيادة في الاهتمام بالاعتبار بخلقها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r2.claim: Mīzān literally names a weighing instrument and by metaphor names justice; here it is the justice God instituted to order creation, as in 57:25.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r3.claim: Waḍʿ, “placing,” metaphorically means appointing justice; after “raising” heaven it forms antithetical wordplay and echoes God's appointing the balance with scripture.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r3.anchor: فالوضع هنا مستعار للجعل فهو كالإنزال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r4.claim: Abū Ṭalḥa uses waḍʿ to mean assigning or designating his beloved property, supporting the sense of appointing a purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r4.anchor: أي اجعلها وعينها لما يدلك الله عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r5.claim: Associating justice with heaven dignifies it as belonging to the realm of truth and virtue and as a divine command sent to earth; the pairing recalls justice in creation and the maxim that heaven and earth stand by justice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p237/r5.anchor: قرن ذلك مع رفع السماء تنويها بشأن العدل بأن نسب إلى العالم العلوي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.claim: The word mīzān and the surrounding verbs, prepositions, and qist jointly support both senses; their converging double meanings are a feature of Qur'anic inimitability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.anchor: كل هذه تظاهرت على إفادة هذه المعاني وهذا من إعجاز القرآن

NAHHAS:v4p303/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p303/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p303/r7.claim: السماء is accusative through an implied verb, coordinating a word governed by one verb with a like verb.
NAHHAS:v4p303/r7.anchor: نصبت بإضمار فعل يعطف ما عمل فيه لفعل على مثله

NAHHAS:v4p303/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p303/r9.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v4p303/r9.claim: Others take الميزان to mean the physical balance used for weighing.
NAHHAS:v4p303/r9.anchor: وقال غيره هو الميزان الذي يوزن به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r12.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r12.claim: Most readers put السماء in the accusative, coordinating with the nearby verb-and-subject clause يسجدان.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r12.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «والسماء رفعها» بالنصب عطفا على الجملة الصغيرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r13.speaker: أبو السمال
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r13.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads السماء in the nominative, coordinating with the larger nominal clause والنجم والشجر يسجدان.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال: «والسماء» بالرفع عطفا على الجملة الكبيرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r14.speaker: مصحف ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r14.claim: Ibn Masʿud's codex reads وخفض الميزان instead of the standard form.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r15.claim: وضع means to establish; most people, including al-Tabari and Mujahid, explain الميزان as justice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r15.anchor: ومعنى: وضع أقر وأثبت، والميزان: العدل فيما قال الطبري ومجاهد وأكثر الناس.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r16.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r16.claim: They interpret الميزان as the familiar weighing scale.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r16.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة: إنه الميزان المعروف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r1.claim: The familiar scale is one instance of the broader metaphor of justice; he takes وضع الميزان here to mean establishing justice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r1.anchor: والميزان المعروف جزء من «الميزان» الذي يعبر به عن العدل.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r1.claim: God raised the sky to sustain living creatures and breathing, and placed wind between sky and earth to refresh creation; without it they would die in distress.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r1.anchor: وإنما فعل ذلك ليحيا الحيوان وتمتد الأنفاس وأجرى الريح بينها وبين الأرض كيما يتروح الخلق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r2.speaker: الأكثرون ومنهم مجاهد والسدي واللغويون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r2.claim: The majority, including Mujāhid, al-Suddī, and linguists, interpret the balance as justice; al-Zajjāj links this to the balancing of things against one another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r2.anchor: أحدها أنه العدل قاله الأكثرون منهم مجاهد والسدي واللغويون قال الزجاج وهذا لأن المعادلة موازنة الأشياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk interpret the balance as the familiar scales by which people give one another their due rights.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه الميزان المعروف ليتناصف الناس في الحقوق قاله الحسن وقتادة والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r4.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl interprets the balance as the Qurʾān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#2/r4.anchor: والثالث أنه القرآن قاله الحسين بن الفضل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r3.claim: The raised heaven and set balance mean justice, as in the sending of messengers with scripture and balance so people uphold justice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r3.anchor: والسماء رفعها ووضع الميزان} يعني: العدل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r25.claim: God raised the sky above the earth; الميزان may be a physical balance used to uphold people's rights.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r25.anchor: والسمآء رفعها } يعني على الأرض . { ووضع الميزان

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r27.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r27.claim: They understand الميزان as justice; Hassan's verse invokes its balance when matters become confused.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r27.anchor: والسدي : أنه العدل ، ومنه قول حسان

MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.claim: Low plants without stems and trees with stems prostrate through their shadows as the sun moves; the sky is raised 500 years above earth, and the balance establishes justice, requiring people not to cheat in measures.
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.anchor: { والنجم } يعني كل نبت ليس له ساق { والشجر } كل نبت له ساق

NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#3/r1.claim: God created the sky raised and supported, making it the source of His judgments and decrees and the abode of angels descending with revelation, a sign of His majesty and sovereignty.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#3/r1.anchor: خلقها مرفوعة ومسموكة حيث جعلها منشأ احكامه ومصدر قضاياه ومسكن ملائكته الذين يهبطون بالوحى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#3/r2.claim: The balance means every instrument for weighing and measuring, such as scales, a steelyard, a measure, or a gauge, placed on earth to govern fairness in people's exchanges.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#3/r2.anchor: كل ما توزن به الاشياء وتعرف مقاديرها من ميزان وقرسطون ومكيال ومقياس

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r1.speaker: أبو السمال
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r1.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads “the heaven” in the nominative as a subject parallel to the preceding nominal clause.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال «والسماء» بالرفع على الابتداء

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r2.claim: The majority read it in the accusative, with an implied verb indicated by what follows.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r2.anchor: الباقون بالنصب على إضمار فعل يدل عليه ما بعده.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r3.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r3.claim: Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Suddi say the balance is justice God established and commanded people to practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r3.anchor: { ووضع الميزان } أي العدل عن مجاهد وقتادة والسدي

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r4.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r4.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl interprets the balance as the Qur'an, which explains what people need.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r4.anchor: وقيل: على هذا الميزان القرآن، لأن فيه بيان ما يحتاج إليه وهو قول الحسين بن الفضل.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r5.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak identify the balance as a physical scale through which people receive just treatment.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة أيضا والضحاك: هو الميزان ذو اللسان الذي يوزن به

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r6.claim: Other interpretations take it as judgment or the scale used to weigh deeds in the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو الحكم. وقيل: أراد وضع الميزان في الآخرة لوزن الأعمال.

SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r1.claim: The common reading puts السماء in the accusative through الاشتغال, observing the latter part of a two-faced clause; it supports Sibawayh's allowance without a resumptive pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r1.anchor: العامة على النصب على الاشتغال مراعا لعجز الجملة التي يسميها النحاة ذات وجهين

SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r2.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r2.claim: He requires a pronoun linking the clause to its opening, unlike the majority; al-Farra reports that almost all read without one.
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r2.anchor: والأخفش يقول: لا بد من ضمير، مثاله: " هند قامت وعمرا أكرمته لأجلها

SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r3.claim: The common ووضع uses a past verb with الميزان as object; Ibrahim reads ووضع with silent ض and الميزان genitive, coordinating it with the object of رفعها.
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r3.anchor: قوله: { ووضع الميزان } العامة على " وضع " فعلا ماضيا. و " الميزان " نصب على المفعول به. وقرأ إبراهيم

SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r4.claim: He reads ووضع الميزان with a silent ض and genitive الميزان, yielding رفع وضع الميزان: giving the balance elevated status for taking rights.
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r4.anchor: وضع الميزان " بسكون الضاد وخفض " الميزان ". وتخريجها: على أنه معطوف على مفعول " رفعها

SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r5.claim: He says the first clauses omit conjunctions as a rebuke by enumeration; conjunction resumes where the related clauses about celestial and earthly pairs are joined.
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r5.anchor: بكت بالجمل الأول واردة على سنن التعديد الذين أنكروا الرحمن وآلاءه كما يبكت منكر أيادي المنعم

SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r6.claim: He grounds the conjunction in paired relations: sun and moon are heavenly, star and tree earthly, heaven and earth companions, and celestial order resembles submission.
SAMIN-DURR:55:7/r6.anchor: إن الشمس والقمر سماويان، والنجم والشجر أرضيان فبينهما تناسب من حيث التقابل

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r1.claim: In the usual reading, “the heaven” is accusative as the object of an understood verb explained by “He raised it”; another reading has it nominative, coordinated with the opening nominal sentence.

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r2.claim: Setting the balance signifies justice; the sequence moves from knowledge and the Qurʾān, the noblest knowledge, to justice and its instrument, the balance.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r2.anchor: فإشارة إلى العدل وفيه لطيفة وهي أنه تعالى بدأ أولا بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r3.claim: The balance is a great blessing because people resent even small losses and would quarrel without transparent, equal measures; justice sustains society, while the common scale's value is easily overlooked.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#2/r3.anchor: فلولا التبيين ثم التساوي لأوقع الشيطان بين الناس البغضاء

STUDYQURAN:55:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:7/r1.speaker: Most commentators
STUDYQURAN:55:7/r1.claim: Most interpret the Balance as justice.
STUDYQURAN:55:7/r1.anchor: The Balance is seen by most as a reference to justice (JJ, Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:55:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:7/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:55:7/r2.claim: Other interpretations identify the Balance with religious law or the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:55:7/r2.anchor: religious law ( al-sharīʿah ), or the Quran itself (Q; see 57:25c)

STUDYQURAN:55:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:7/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:7/r3.claim: The Balance can also signify honoring the balance and harmony of the created order.
STUDYQURAN:55:7/r3.anchor: It can also be seen as a reference to honoring the balance and harmony of the created order.

STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.claim: Repeating the Balance three times underscores justice as fundamental to divine creation and human transactions.
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.anchor: the fact that it is here thrice mentioned indicates the fundamental importance of justice

STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that the heavens and earth are founded on justice; no grading is given.
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.anchor: The Prophet is reported to have said,“The heavens and the earth are founded upon justice.”

TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r1.claim: Interpreters disagree whether al-najm is low-growing vegetation or a star; all agree the tree is what stands on a trunk. Ibn Abbas, Saʿid, al-Suddi, and Sufyan support vegetation, while Mujahid and Qatada say star.
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r1.anchor: وقال آخرون: عنى بالنجم في هذا الموضع: نجم السماء

TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari prefers vegetation because it pairs naturally with trees: standing trees and ground-covering plants both prostrate, as do all God's diverse creatures.
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r2.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: عنى بالنجم: ما نجم من الأرض

TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the plant spreads over the earth.
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {والنجم} [النجم: 1] قال: «ما يبسط على الأرض»

TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r4.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r4.claim: Saʿid defines it as vegetation spread along the ground and notes Arabs call couch grass najm.
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r4.anchor: عن جعفر، عن سعيد، في قوله: {والنجم} [النجم: 1] قال: «النجم كل شيء ذهب مع الأرض فرشا»

TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets al-najm as a star in the sky.
TAB-FULL:v22p173#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {والنجم} [النجم: 1] قال: «نجم السماء»

TAB-FULL:v22p178/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p178/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p178/r1.claim: God established justice among His creatures on earth; the reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah says “lowered the balance,” and lowering and setting are close in Arabic.
TAB-FULL:v22p178/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {ووضع الميزان} [الرحمن: 7] قال: «العدل»

TAB-FULL:v22p178/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p178/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p178/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the balance as justice.
TAB-FULL:v22p178/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {ووضع الميزان} [الرحمن: 7] قال: «العدل»

ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r1.claim: God raised the sky above the earth and held it so that it would not fall onto the earth.
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r1.anchor: المعنى رفعها فوق الأرض وأمسكها أن تقع على الأرض

ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r2.claim: He established the balance so that people could settle disputes fairly with one another.
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r2.anchor: ووضع الميزان لينتصف بعض الناس من بعض

ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r3.claim: An alternative interpretation takes the balance as justice, since equating things is a kind of balancing.
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r3.anchor: وقيل: الميزان ههنا العدل، لأن المعادلة موازنة الأشياء.

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r1.claim: If sky means the upper direction, God created it elevated; if it means the celestial bodies, He positioned them above earth after separation; the elevation is physical either way, or also spiritual if angelic stations and revelation's sources are included.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r1.anchor: والرفع على أي حال رفع حسي. وإن كان المراد ما يشمل منازل الملائكة الكرام ومصادر الأمر الإلهي والوحي فالرفع معنوي

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r2.claim: Mizan broadly means any standard for measuring or judging matters, including beliefs, speech, deeds, and the scales for weights; this is wider than the reported views of justice alone or a physical scale alone.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r2.anchor: المراد بالميزان كل ما يوزن أي يقدر به الشيء أعم من أن يكون عقيدة أو قولا أو فعلا ومن مصاديقه الميزان الذي يوزن به الأثقال

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r3.claim: One reported interpretation identifies the balance with justice that lets people treat things equally and give each right-holder their due.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد بالميزان العدل أي وضع الله العدل بينكم لتسووا به بين الأشياء بإعطاء كل ذي حق حقه

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r4.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies the balance simply as the scale used to weigh heavy goods.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد الميزان الذي يوزن به الأثقال والمعنى الأول أوسع وأشمل

TABRISI:55:6-10/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:6-10/r7.claim: God raised the sky above the earth as a sign of His perfect power.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r7.anchor: أي ورفع السماء رفعها فوق الأرض دل سبحانه بذلك على كمال قدرته

THALABI:v9p177#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r8.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v9p177#3/r8.claim: Mujahid interprets the balance as justice.

THALABI:v9p177#3/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r9.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وقتادة
THALABI:v9p177#3/r9.claim: Hasan, al-Dahhak, and Qatada identify the balance as the instrument used to weigh and achieve fairness.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن والضحاك وقتادة: هو الذي يوزن به ليوصل به الإنصاف والانتصاف

THALABI:v9p177#3/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r10.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v9p177#3/r10.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl interprets the balance as the Quran; weighing fundamentally means estimation.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r10.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: هو القرآن، وأصل الوزن التقدير.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r1.speaker: مقاتل وغيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r1.claim: Muqātil and others say God raised the heavens five hundred years above the earth and held them from falling onto it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r1.anchor: رفعها فوق الأرض مسيرة خمسمائة عام وأمسكها أن تقع على الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r2.claim: One interpretation of the balance is the familiar weighing instrument, set among people to let each obtain justice from the other.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r2.anchor: يعني الذي يزن به الناس وضعه عدلا بينهم لينتصف بعض الناس من بعض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk likewise identify the balance as the scales by which claims are weighed fairly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r3.anchor: وهو قول الحسن وقتادة والضحاك (¬6)، قالوا: هو الذي يوزن به ليوصل به إلى الإنصاف والانتصاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r4.claim: The language scholars treat the weighing instrument as a blessing and guidance, since without it many rights could not be secured.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r4.anchor: أهل المعاني: وهذا تنبيه على النعمة فيه والهداية إليه، ولولا الميزان لتعذر الوصول إلى كثير من الحقوق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās understands the balance metaphorically as justice among people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r5.anchor: يعني العدل في الأرض بين الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r6.claim: Mujāhid also interprets the balance as justice.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r7.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the balance here is justice because equalizing things is a kind of weighing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r7.anchor: الميزان هاهنا العدل؛ لأن المعادلة موازنة الأشياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r8.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r8.claim: On the justice interpretation, the verse commands justice, as the following order to establish the weighing with equity indicates.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p137/r8.anchor: صاحب النظم: على هذا القول: تأويله أمر بالعدل يدل هذا قوله تعالى

ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r1.claim: God raised the skies and established a measure for all things.
ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r1.anchor: And the skies has He raised high, and has devised [for all things] a measure

ASAD-NOTES:55:7#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:7#n3/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:7#n3/r1.claim: Following Zamakhshari, Asad reads mizan broadly as measure or measuring by any means, in concrete and abstract senses.
ASAD-NOTES:55:7#n3/r1.anchor: The noun mizan, usually denoting a "balance", has here the more general connotation of "measure" or "measuring" by any means whatsoever (Zamakhshari)

ASAD-NOTES:55:7#n3/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:7#n3/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:7#n3/r2.claim: Asad links this parabolic use of mizan with 42:17 and 57:25.
ASAD-NOTES:55:7#n3/r2.anchor: Cf. also the parabolic use of the term mza~ in 42:17 and 57:25.

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r1.claim: In the Turkish rendering, Elmalılı describes the heaven as beautiful and says God gave it elevation while placing the balance.

ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r3.claim: The syntax first suppresses the object of raised and then resumes it with a pronoun, foregrounding heaven and specifically emphasizing the act of raising it.

ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r4.claim: Heaven means the encompassing cosmos and its celestial bodies; its elevation is its high creation, chiefly physical though also open to a figurative spiritual sense.
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r4.anchor: “Semâ”dan murad, bütün ecrâmıyla üzerimizde yükselen muhît-i âlemdir

ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r5.claim: The visible height of heaven shows the greatness of the Rahman's creative mercy and His exaltedness above directions and place, making Him worthy of prostration and reverence.
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r5.anchor: semânın böyle rif‘ati onu yükselten Rahmân’ın sun‘u rahmetinin yüksekliğini

ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r11.claim: The first mizan is the universal equilibrium law, most visibly gravity, underlying scales and weights and operating throughout celestial and terrestrial bodies; in a wider reading it also covers chemical and spiritual relations as justice.
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r11.anchor: bütün eşya arasındaki muvâzene-i umûmiye kanunudur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r8.claim: The sky may mean the vast cosmic space containing galaxies and celestial bodies moving in an ordered way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r8.anchor: milyarlarca galaksi ve gök cisminin içinde yer aldığı ve belli bir düzene göre hareket ettiği kozmik uzayın kastedildiği söylenebilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r9.claim: Raising the sky can mean its literal height above us or a metaphorical spiritual elevation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r9.anchor: bize nisbetle yüksekte olması yahut mecazî anlamda düşünülüp mânevî bir yüksekliğe sahip olması şeklinde yorumlanabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r10.claim: Either reading points to God's supreme majesty and the fact that only God deserves worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r10.anchor: Her iki mâna, bizi, bunu sağlayan Allah Teâlâ’nın yüceler yücesi olduğu, secde ve kulluk edilmeye lâyık başka mâbud bulunmadığı gerçeğine götürür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r12.claim: The first occurrence of mizan suggests the universal balance law that allows the cosmos and all its processes to function as an ordered system.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r12.anchor: Yüce Allah evrende denge kanununu koymuştur; bütün varlık ve oluşlar arasında, evrenin belirli bir sistem dahilinde yürümesini sağlayan bir genel denge mevcuttur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r13.speaker: Taberî ve İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r13.claim: Many exegetes understand mizan here as justice, including Tabari and Ibn Atiyya.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r13.anchor: “adalet” anlamının kastedildiği kanaatindedir (meselâ bk. Taberî, XXVII, 118; İbn Atıyye, V, 224)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.claim: The first signs emphasized show that God cherishes justice and rejects whatever violates justice and equity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.anchor: First and foremost are mentioned those signs and manifestations which point to the fact that the Almighty greatly cherishes justice and does not approve anything contrary to justice and equity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r4.claim: God raised the immense sky like a roof without columns and made it so balanced that it has no visible fault, as other passages also affirm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r4.anchor: the Almighty has raised this unfathomable roof without any columns. No one can have an idea of its vastness.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r1.claim: The sky’s balance is maintained by invisible gravitational columns.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r1.anchor: the Almighty has used gravitational columns which cannot be observed.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p302/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p302/r1.speaker: أبو السمال
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p302/r1.claim: He reads والسماء رفعها with nominative السماء, making a full nominal sentence coordinated with والنجم والشجر يسجدان; the common accusative instead coordinates on يسجدان with an understood verb رفع.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p302/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p302/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p302/r2.claim: Against Abu al-Hasan's ban on coordinating clauses with unlike syntactic positions, Abu al-Fath argues an unspoken case position has no force; he supports this with the accusative reading and analogous omitted pronouns.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p302/r2.anchor: كما أن الضمير في اسم الفاعل لما لم يظهر إلى اللفظ جرى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r1.claim: God made the sky raised, source of His decrees and dwelling of angels bearing revelation, showing His majesty and sovereignty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r1.anchor: والسماء رفعها: أي خلقها مرفوعة، حيث جعلها مصدر قضاياه ومسكن ملائكته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r2.claim: Most read السماء accusative by الاشتغال; Abu al-Sammal reads it nominative. Most parse ووضع as a past verb establishing the balance, while Ibrahim reads it as a genitive verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: والسماء، بالنصب على الاشتغال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r3.claim: They define الميزان as any measuring instrument and as God's just standard in taking and giving.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r3.anchor: والظاهر أنه كل ما يوزن به الأشياء وتعرف مقاديرها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r4.speaker: مجاهد والطبري والأكثرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r4.claim: They interpret الميزان as justice, which encompasses weighing instruments.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد والطبري والأكثرون: الميزان: العدل، وتكون الآلات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r5.claim: After the Qur'an as highest knowledge comes the balance that sets affairs right, as in the book and balance sent for people to learn and obey.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r5.anchor: بدأ أولا بالعلم، فذكر ما فيه أشرف أنواع العلوم وهو القرآن ثم ذكر ما به التعديل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r1.claim: The sky was created raised from the start, not first low and then lifted; the primary sense is physical elevation, though it can also include its rank as the source of divine decrees, commands, and angelic presence.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r1.anchor: خلقها مرفوعة ابتداءا لا أنها كانت مخفوضة ورفعها والظاهر أن المراد برفعها الرفع الصوري

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r2.speaker: أبو السمال
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads “the sky” in the nominative as the subject of a nominal clause coordinated with the preceding nominal clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r2.anchor: وقراأبو السمال ( والسماء ) بالرفع على الأبتداء ولا إشكال فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r3.claim: The accusative reading implies an elided verb, “He raises the sky”; attaching it to the larger clause about stars and trees creates an undesirable mismatch of nominal and verbal clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r3.anchor: السماء فتكون الجملة فعلية فإن عطفت على جملة النجم والشجر يسجدان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r4.claim: Abu Ali attaches the phrase to the smaller clause about the stars and trees, arguing that a conjunct need not preserve its counterpart's grammatical form.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r4.anchor: لا يلزم في المعطوف على الشيء أن يعتبر فيه حال ذلك الشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r5.claim: Other grammarians prefer the larger attachment, allowing the contrast because it carries a rhetorical point; al-Tibi favors coordination with the sun and moon clause to distinguish continued subjection from emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r5.anchor: قال الطيبي : الظاهر أن يعطف على جملة ( الشمس والقمر بحسبان )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r6.claim: Alusi also notes the broader grammatical question of coordinating onto a clause that itself has both nominal and verbal faces.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#2/r6.anchor: والكلام فيما يتعلق بالرفع والنصب فيما إذا ولي العاطف جملة ذات وجهين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r1.claim: Setting the balance means instituting and commanding justice: giving each deserving recipient their due and every right its fulfillment orders and stabilizes the world.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r1.anchor: شرع العدل وأمر به بأن وفر على كل مستعد مستحقه ووفى في كل ذي حق حقه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r2.claim: A Prophetic saying states that the heavens and earth stand through justice; some interpret this as referring only to their inhabitants, but Alusi prefers the entire created order.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r2.anchor: كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : بالعدل قامت السماوات والأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r3.claim: Alusi rejects limiting the Prophetic statement to adjudication between people: it means God's justice in giving each thing its created form and due.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r3.anchor: بل المراد به عدل الله عز وجل وإعطاؤه سبحانه كل شيء خلقه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r4.claim: Mujahid, al-Tabari, and most interpreters take the balance as a metaphor for justice; Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak take it as the known measuring device and similar instruments.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r4.anchor: وتفسير الميزان بما ذكر هو المروي عن مجاهد والطبري والأكثرين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r5.claim: On the instrument reading, the balance is placed on earth for human affairs, judgments, and the commanded fairness of giving and taking; the term may be figurative, literal, or a name for any means of measuring.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r5.anchor: والضحاك أن المرادبه ما يعرف به مقادير الأشياء من الآلة المعروفة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r6.claim: The physical balance reading better fits the following command and forms a contrast with the sky's raising; Alusi nevertheless prefers the justice reading as more comprehensive and beneficial.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r6.anchor: ورجح القولان الأخيران بأن ما بعد أشد ملاءمة لهما وبين الوضع والرفع عليهما تقابل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r7.claim: Abdullah's reading has “and lowered the balance.”
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101#3/r7.anchor: وقد قرأعبد الله وخفض الميزان والأول بانه أتم فائدة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r1.claim: The sky is raised above the earth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says the scale means justice, as confirmed by the command not to transgress it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r3.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak take the scale as the physical weighing instrument that enables fairness; its basic sense is measurement.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة والضحاك: أراد به الذي يوزن به ليوصل به إلى الإنصاف والانتصاف،

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r1.claim: God created heaven elevated in place and rank as the source of decrees and rulings and the abode of angels; another reading makes al-samāʾ nominative as a subject.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r1.anchor: خلقها مرفوعة محلا ومرتبة، فإنها منشأ أقضيته ومتنزل أحكامه

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r2.claim: The balance may mean justice, giving each deserving recipient their due and every rights-holder their right, thereby ordering the world.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r2.anchor: العدل بأن وفر على كل مستعد مستحقه، ووفى كل ذي حق حقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r3.claim: A Prophetic saying is cited that justice established the heavens and earth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r3.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام " بالعدل قامت السموات والأرض "

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r4.claim: Alternatively, the balance is an instrument such as scales or a measure that reveals amounts and equitable rights on earth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r4.anchor: أو ما يعرف به مقادير الأشياء من ميزان ومكيال ونحوهما

BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r3.claim: God’s raising of the sky identifies Him as its effective cause; its ordered balance of seasons and measured precipitation manifests justice and sustains the earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r3.anchor: ودلنا على أنه شرع لنا مثل ذلك العدل لتقوم أحوالنا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r4.claim: The balance means justice that orders both cosmic realms; the Qur’an is a balance for knowledge and the scale a balance for sensible things.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r4.anchor: العدل الذي بدر به الخافقين من الموازنة وهي المعادلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r16.claim: God raised and made the sky firm as the source of His judgments, decrees, commands, and prohibitions, and as the dwelling of angels who bring revelation; this signals His majesty and sovereignty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r16.anchor: خلقها مرفوعة مسموكة ، حيث جعلها منشأ أحكامه ، ومصدر قضاياه ، ومتنزل أوامره ونواهيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r17.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r17.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading has “and He lowered the balance” in place of “and He set the balance.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r17.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله ( وخفض الميزان )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.claim: The balance includes every instrument for weighing or measuring quantities; God placed it on earth for judgments, transactions, and the fair treatment He enjoined in giving and taking.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.anchor: وأراد به كل ما توزن به الأشياء وتعرف مقاديرها من ميزان وقرسطون ومكيال ومقياس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r21.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r21.claim: A reading gives al-samāʾ in the nominative.

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r4.claim: The raised heaven is paired with the placed earth, continuing the sequence of celestial signs before earthly ones.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r4.anchor: والسماء رفعها } ( الرحمن : 7 ) وفي مقابلتها : { والارض وضعها } ( الرحمن : 10 )

BURSEVI:v9p238/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238/r1.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v9p238/r1.claim: Al-Kashifi gives two glosses for setting up the balance: God established the scales, or inspired people with the way to make them.
BURSEVI:v9p238/r1.anchor: قال الكاشفي : ووضع الميزان وبيا فريد يا منزل كردانيد ترازورا يا الهام داد خلق

BURSEVI:v9p238/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p238/r2.claim: The balance was established so people could act justly and receive fair treatment; the author dates the institution of measures to Noah's time, saying there had been no measures, weights, or cubits before him.
BURSEVI:v9p238/r2.anchor: ليتوصل به إلا الإنصاف والانتصاف وكان ذلك في زمان نوح عليه السلام إذ لم يكن قبله كيل ووزن وذراع

TABRISI:55:6/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6/r11.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:55:6/r11.claim: Ibn Jinnī prefers the noncanonical nominative because it coordinates a full nominal clause with the preceding nominal clause; the common accusative attaches to يسجدان and implies a second verb, رفع السماء.
TABRISI:55:6/r11.anchor: قال ابن جني الرفع هنا أظهر من قراءة الجماعة

BURHAN:v3p197/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p197/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p197/r9.claim: The general omitted-governor category covers accusatives licensed by an expressed, understood, or estimated verb; the cited constructions illustrate its varied triggers.
BURHAN:v3p197/r9.anchor: والعام كل منصوب دل عليه الفعل لفظا أو معنى أو تقديرا ويحذف لأسباب

BURHAN:v3p197/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p197/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p197/r10.claim: One reason to omit the verb is that another expression explains it; examples include إياي فارهبون, والسماء رفعها, and conditional clauses.
BURHAN:v3p197/r10.anchor: أحدها أن يكون مفسرا كقوله تعالى

BURHAN:v3p376/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p376/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p376/r3.claim: One kind of verbal matching makes the second expression resemble the first; examples include a neighboring-word reading in ablution and the transition from the trees' prostration to the heaven's raising.
BURHAN:v3p376/r3.anchor: أحدهما وهو الأكثر المشاكلة بالثاني للأول نحو أخذه ما قدم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r1.claim: Calling a camel shepherd’s staff weak or firm can serve the same end, good care: weakness suggests gentleness, while firmness suggests effective control without repeated blows.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r1.anchor: فإنهما يرجعان إلى غرض واحد وهو حسن الرعية والعمل بما يصلحها ويحسن أثره عليها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r2.claim: The ‘weak staff’ means the shepherd is gentle and chooses a soft stick rather than hurting the animals needlessly.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r2.anchor: أنه رفيق بها مشفق عليها لا يقصد من حمل العصا أن يوجعها بالضرب من غير فائدة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r3.claim: The ‘firm staff’ means the shepherd knows how to manage the herd, steer it from harmful pasture, and keep it together through disciplined leadership.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r3.anchor: أنه جيد الضبط لها عارف بسياستها في الرعي يزجرها عن المراعى التي لا تحمد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r4.claim: A different line calling someone firm of staff and aloof from flirtation does not make the same point as the shepherding examples.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r4.anchor: وقال آخر صلب العصا جاف عن التغزل فهذا لم يبين ما بينه الآخر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r5.claim: ‘A finger’ can indicate a shepherd’s skillful effect because delicate work depends on precise movement of the fingers; it is not a general independent word for an effect.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r5.anchor: فدلوا عليه بالأصبع لأن الأعمال الدقيقة لها اختصاص بالأصابع

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r6.claim: Ordinary usage confirms the link: people do not call traces of a house ‘its fingers’ or describe an effect generically as a good or bad finger.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r6.anchor: لا يقولون رأيت أصابع الدار بمعنى آثار الدار وله أصبع حسنة وأصبع قبيحة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r8.claim: The same principle applies to ‘hand’ when it signifies a benefaction through the hand’s characteristic action; a bare phrase such as ‘acquired a blessing’ carries no such image.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r8.anchor: كذلك ينبغي أن تعلم ذلك في اليد لقيام هذه العلة فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r7.claim: The passage pairs creation of heaven and Earth after the paired opposites of sun and moon, then stars and trees, and returns to predicating a verb of the subject as in the opening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r7.anchor: اطرد في هذه الآية أسلوب المقابلة بين ما يشبه الضدين بعد مقابلة ذكر الشمس والقمر بذكر النجمم والشجر ، فجيء بذكر خلق السماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r8.claim: Raising the heaven entails creating it; the wording highlights the marvelous creation and means that it was made raised without pillars.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r8.anchor: ورفع السماء يقتضي خلقها . وذكر رفعها لأنه محل العبرة بالخلق العجيب .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r9.claim: The phrase means creating the heaven in a raised state, like telling a tailor to make a shirt pocket wide; its use for exalted rank also gives the wording a literal and figurative sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r9.anchor: كما يقال للخياط : وسع جيب القميص ، أي خطه واسعا على أن في مجرد الرفع إيذانا بسمو المنزلة وشرفها

MUJAHID:v2p639#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p639#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p639#3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the balance God set as justice.
MUJAHID:v2p639#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ والسماء رفعها ووضع الميزان ﴾ قال يقول وضع العدل
